sources.title: Refunds and cancellations for App Store and Google Play purchases
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the App Store or Google Play
sources.body:
Subscriptions bought through the App Store or Google Play are billed by Apple or Google, not by Nebula.

- Nebula **cannot** issue refunds for these purchases and cannot see the customer's card details.
- The customer must request the refund from the store (see help articles `help-refund-app-store` and `help-refund-google-play`). The store decides; agents must not promise an outcome.
- Cancellation must also be done in the store's subscription settings. Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription.
- If the customer is unsure where they paid: ask them to check their bank statement. "APPLE.COM/BILL" or "Google Play" means a store purchase; "NEBULA" or "OBRIO" means a website purchase.

sources.title: Refund policy for website purchases
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the Nebula website
sources.body:
Applies only to purchases made on the Nebula website (billed by Nebula, not by Apple or Google).

- **Duplicate charges** (same plan charged twice in one billing period): always refund the duplicate in full. No approval needed.
- **Charged after cancellation**: if the cancellation is visible in the admin panel before the charge date, refund in full. No approval needed.
- **Trial converted to a paid subscription**: full refund if the customer asks within 48 hours of the first paid charge AND has not used any paid feature since the conversion.
- **Accidental or unwanted purchase**: full refund within 14 days of the charge if the customer used at most 3 paid readings/reports in that period.
- **Anything else** (older than 14 days, heavy usage, partial months): no refund by default. The agent may offer bonus credits instead. Exceptions need team lead approval.
- Refunds above **$50** in total for one customer need team lead approval.

Refunds return to the original payment method within 5–10 business days. Never promise a faster timeline.

sources.title: Investigating unexpected or duplicate charges
sources.body:
1. Ask for (or look up) the charge date, amount and the name on the bank statement.
2. "APPLE.COM/BILL" or "Google Play" → store purchase, follow `policy-refund-store`.
3. "NEBULA"/"OBRIO" → find the charges in the admin panel. Identify the type: trial conversion, renewal, duplicate, or charge after cancellation.
4. Apply `policy-refund-web` for that type. Explain in plain words what the charge was for.
5. Make sure auto-renewal is cancelled if the customer does not want the subscription (`sop-cancel-web-subscription`).

sources.title: How to cancel a website subscription (agent steps)
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the Nebula website
sources.body:
1. Find the customer in the admin panel by email.
2. Check the subscription source. If it says "App Store" or "Google Play", stop: the customer must cancel in the store (`policy-refund-store`).
3. Click **Subscription → Cancel auto-renewal**. Access stays active until the end of the paid period.
4. Confirm to the customer: the date access ends, and that no further charges will be made.
5. If the customer was charged after an earlier cancellation attempt, check `policy-refund-web` for a refund.

sources.condition: applies only if paid via the App Store or Google Play
sources.body:
Subscriptions bought through the App Store or Google Play are billed by Apple or Google, not by Nebula.

- Nebula **cannot** issue refunds for these purchases and cannot see the customer's card details.
- The customer must request the refund from the store (see help articles `help-refund-app-store` and `help-refund-google-play`). The store decides; agents must not promise an outcome.
- Cancellation must also be done in the store's subscription settings. Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription.
- If the customer is unsure where they paid: ask them to check their bank statement. "APPLE.COM/BILL" or "Google Play" means a store purchase; "NEBULA" or "OBRIO" means a website purchase.

sources.title: Refund policy for website purchases
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the Nebula website
sources.body:
Applies only to purchases made on the Nebula website (billed by Nebula, not by Apple or Google).

- **Duplicate charges** (same plan charged twice in one billing period): always refund the duplicate in full. No approval needed.
- **Charged after cancellation**: if the cancellation is visible in the admin panel before the charge date, refund in full. No approval needed.
- **Trial converted to a paid subscription**: full refund if the customer asks within 48 hours of the first paid charge AND has not used any paid feature since the conversion.
- **Accidental or unwanted purchase**: full refund within 14 days of the charge if the customer used at most 3 paid readings/reports in that period.
- **Anything else** (older than 14 days, heavy usage, partial months): no refund by default. The agent may offer bonus credits instead. Exceptions need team lead approval.
- Refunds above **$50** in total for one customer need team lead approval.

Refunds return to the original payment method within 5–10 business days. Never promise a faster timeline.

sources.title: Crisis protocol (self-harm or emotional crisis signals)
sources.body:
Use whenever a customer expresses hopelessness, wanting to die, self-harm, or not being able to go on, in any language.

1. **Respond personally within 1 hour.** Do not use templates, macros or AI drafts.
2. Lead with care, not with the account issue: acknowledge what they wrote, tell them they matter and that you are glad they reached out.
3. Share crisis resources: local emergency number if they are in immediate danger, and https://findahelpline.com to find a free, confidential helpline in their country.
4. **Do not** give readings, predictions or advice about their future, and do not suggest an advisor chat.
5. Resolve any billing question gently and generously (refund per policy without arguing), but only after the care message.
6. Notify the team lead on duty and add the "crisis" tag; the team lead checks in on the conversation.

sources.title: Account and personal data deletion (GDPR)
sources.body:
- Every deletion request must be completed within **30 days** (GDPR). Log the request date.
- Verify identity first: the request must come from the account email, or the customer must confirm via the verification link (see `sop-identity-verification`).
- Deletion is permanent: readings, chat history, credits and birth data are erased. Tell the customer this before confirming.
- Active website subscriptions must be cancelled as part of the deletion. App Store / Google Play subscriptions must be cancelled by the customer in the store; deletion does not stop store billing.
- Never ask the customer *why* they want deletion and never try to talk them out of it.

sources.title: Chargeback and dispute threats
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the Nebula website
sources.body:
When a customer mentions a chargeback, bank dispute, lawyer or consumer authority:

1. Hand the ticket to senior billing the same business day (`policy-escalation-matrix`).
2. Do not argue, do not threaten account closure, and do not discourage the customer from contacting their bank.
3. Check the charge against `policy-refund-web`. If a refund is allowed, offer it clearly; a resolved refund usually prevents the dispute.
4. If a chargeback was already filed, do not refund separately (it would be a double refund); senior billing handles the dispute response.

sources.title: Refunds and cancellations for App Store and Google Play purchases
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the App Store or Google Play
sources.body:
Subscriptions bought through the App Store or Google Play are billed by Apple or Google, not by Nebula.

- Nebula **cannot** issue refunds for these purchases and cannot see the customer's card details.
- The customer must request the refund from the store (see help articles `help-refund-app-store` and `help-refund-google-play`). The store decides; agents must not promise an outcome.
- Cancellation must also be done in the store's subscription settings. Deleting the app does not cancel the subscription.
- If the customer is unsure where they paid: ask them to check their bank statement. "APPLE.COM/BILL" or "Google Play" means a store purchase; "NEBULA" or "OBRIO" means a website purchase.

sources.title: Refund policy for website purchases
sources.condition: applies only if paid via the Nebula website
sources.body:
Applies only to purchases made on the Nebula website (billed by Nebula, not by Apple or Google).

- **Duplicate charges** (same plan charged twice in one billing period): always refund the duplicate in full. No approval needed.
- **Charged after cancellation**: if the cancellation is visible in the admin panel before the charge date, refund in full. No approval needed.
- **Trial converted to a paid subscription**: full refund if the customer asks within 48 hours of the first paid charge AND has not used any paid feature since the conversion.
- **Accidental or unwanted purchase**: full refund within 14 days of the charge if the customer used at most 3 paid readings/reports in that period.
- **Anything else** (older than 14 days, heavy usage, partial months): no refund by default. The agent may offer bonus credits instead. Exceptions need team lead approval.
- Refunds above **$50** in total for one customer need team lead approval.

Refunds return to the original payment method within 5–10 business days. Never promise a faster timeline.

sources.title: Investigating unexpected or duplicate charges
sources.body:
1. Ask for (or look up) the charge date, amount and the name on the bank statement.
2. "APPLE.COM/BILL" or "Google Play" → store purchase, follow `policy-refund-store`.
3. "NEBULA"/"OBRIO" → find the charges in the admin panel. Identify the type: trial conversion, renewal, duplicate, or charge after cancellation.
4. Apply `policy-refund-web` for that type. Explain in plain words what the charge was for.
5. Make sure auto-renewal is cancelled if the customer does not want the subscription (`sop-cancel-web-subscription`).

sources.title: Credits, bonus credits and credit refunds
sources.body:
Credits are used to pay for chats with advisors. Credit restores work the same for every billing channel (website, App Store, Google Play), so there is no need to ask where the customer paid.

- Credits are **not refundable to a card**. Credit problems are resolved by restoring credits to the account.
- **Bonus credits** from an offer are added within 24 hours of purchase. If they are missing after 24 hours, the agent restores them.
- **Restore credits for a session** when: the advisor's average reply time was over 3 minutes, the advisor did not answer the question, or the session ended because of a technical failure.
- **Reading quality** complaints ("inaccurate", "generic"): one goodwill restore per customer per 30 days, up to the credits spent on that session.
- Agents can restore up to **50 credits** without approval. More than 50 credits needs team lead approval.

sources.title: How credits work
sources.body:
Credits pay for chats with advisors; the advisor's rate per minute is shown before you start.
- Credit packs and bonus offers appear in your balance within a few minutes; bonus credits can take up to 24 hours.
- Credits do not expire.
- If something went wrong in a chat (the advisor didn't answer, or the app crashed), contact support and we will review the session.
